intended_object: The open subset B = {z ∈ ℂ ∖ {0,1} : Re z > 0} of the thrice-punctured sphere ℂ ∖ {0,1}. In ℂ this is the right half-plane with the puncture 1 removed. It is one of the two sets of the standard open cover used with Seifert–van Kampen; the other is A = {Re z < 1}. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body is `{z | 0 < (z : ℂ).re}`, a subset of the subtype `{z : ℂ // z ≠ 0 ∧ z ≠ 1}`. This is exactly the half-plane Re z > 0, restricted to the thrice-punctured sphere. The point 0 is not in the half-plane anyway, so the only point actually removed is 1, as the docstring says. The library's lemma `image_coe_rightOpen` proves that the image of this set in ℂ is `{0 < re z} \ {1}`. Other lemmas in the file show that the set is open, that it covers the space together with `leftOpen`, and that the intersection of the two sets is the strip 0 < Re z < 1. All of this matches the standard cover. The set is a specific concrete object in a specific space, so it is not too narrow, and Mathlib has no counterpart for it.
